content: Metoclopramide functions by inhibiting the action of dopamine, a naturally occurring substance in the body. This medication is not recommended for use in children due to an increased risk of severe side effects, such as muscle spasms or uncontrolled muscle movements. Before starting metoclopramide and each time you receive a refill, carefully read the Medication Guide provided by your pharmacist. Take this medication orally as directed by your physician, typically up to four times daily, 30 minutes before meals and at bedtime. If you are using the liquid form of this medication, measure the dose accurately using a special measuring device or spoon. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition, response to treatment, age, and any other medications you may be taking. If heartburn occurs only at specific times, such as after an evening meal, your doctor may advise taking a single dose before those times instead of throughout the day. For the treatment of diabetic gastroparesis, this medication is usually prescribed for 2 to 8 weeks until your gastrointestinal function improves. This condition may recur intermittently, and your doctor may instruct you to resume the medication when symptoms reappear and discontinue it once you feel better. To maximize the benefits of this medication, take it regularly as prescribed. Abruptly stopping metoclopramide may result in withdrawal symptoms, such as dizziness, nervousness, or headaches. To minimize withdrawal risks, your doctor may gradually reduce your dosage. Withdrawal symptoms are more likely if you have been using metoclopramide for an extended period or at high doses. Common side effects include drowsiness, dizziness, fatigue, difficulty sleeping, agitation, headaches, and diarrhea. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks of side effects. Metoclopramide may elevate blood pressure and, in rare cases, cause a severe condition known as neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS). Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. Before taking metoclopramide, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may cause dizziness or drowsiness, and consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages, as some liquid formulations of this medication may contain alcohol. Exercise caution if you have diabetes, alcohol dependence, liver disease, or any condition requiring limited alcohol intake. If you have diabetes, this medication may make it more challenging to control your blood sugar levels. Monitor your blood sugar regularly as directed and share the results with your doctor. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience high or low blood sugar levels. Children may be more susceptible to the side effects of this medication, particularly muscle spasms or uncontrolled muscle movements. Older adults may also be more sensitive to its effects, including drowsiness, tardive dyskinesia, and Parkinson’s-like muscle problems. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. Metoclopramide passes into breast milk and may have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Metoclopramide accelerates the movement of food and medication through the stomach, which may affect the absorption of certain drugs. Check the labels of all your medications, such as allergy or cough-and-cold products, as they may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and/or medical tests, such as endoscopy for ulcers, may be conducted while you are taking this medication. Ensure you attend all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
